lines.en: Today we make scrambled eggs. **First**, crack two eggs into a bowl.
lines.pt: Hoje vamos fazer ovos mexidos. Primeiro, quebre dois ovos numa tigela.

lines.en: **Then add** a little salt and **mix** well.
lines.pt: Depois, adicione um pouco de sal e misture bem.

lines.en: Can I mix with a fork?
Yes! **Add** one spoon of butter to a hot pan.
lines.pt: Pode! Adicione uma colher de manteiga numa frigideira quente.

lines.en: **Pour** the eggs in. **Stir** slowly for two minutes.
lines.pt: Despeje os ovos. Mexa devagar por dois minutos.

lines.en: They look good! Is that all?
**Finally**, put them on a plate. Enjoy!
lines.pt: Por fim, coloque no prato. Bom apetite!

pages.title: Cultural snapshot — Life in the USA
pages.intro: American recipes use special words and measures. Look at the cards and guess.

cards.note: “Add the salt. Mix well.” The verb comes first, with no “you”.
US recipes often use cups, tablespoons and teaspoons instead of grams.
Many ovens use Fahrenheit: 350°F is about 175°C.

qs.q: What kind of sentence is in a recipe?
qs.pt: Que tipo de frase tem numa receita?

levels.A2: A command with a verb first: Mix the eggs.
levels.B1: Recipes use the imperative: Add, mix, stir.
levels.B2: Recipes use the imperative with no subject, which keeps instructions short and clear.
Cups and spoons rather than grams, and Fahrenheit for the oven.

levels.A2: First, crack the eggs. Then add salt.

pages.compare: Brazilian recipes also use commands (“misture”, “adicione”), and many use grams. What measures do you use at home?

pages.title: Level up — the same situation from A1 to C2
pages.intro: You do not need six different methods: the structure stays, while language complexity and autonomy grow.

ladder.goal: Name the steps with single words.

ladder.say: First, crack two eggs. Then add salt.
After you add the salt, mix it well so the eggs are smooth.
Make sure the pan is hot before you pour the eggs in, otherwise they will stick.
Once the butter has melted, lower the heat and fold the eggs gently until they set.
Take them off the heat a moment early; they’ll carry on cooking on the plate.

pages.note: This progression is illustrative: complex sentences do not define a level on their own. CEFR also considers comprehension, autonomy, fluency, accuracy, interaction and appropriateness.
